graphEvents.label: Where purpose is written and validated per level
Purpose written once in PROBLEM & PURPOSE
Phase parent exempt from required-anchor check

label: Problem and purpose are written once per packet, in one section at every authored level: '## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE' with '### Problem Statement' and '### Purpose' (core, phase-parent and research-record templates).

User need has no dedicated authored field at Levels 1-2: the As-a/I-want/so-that surface ('## 11. USER STORIES') is emitted only for level:3,3+; below Level 3 the user need survives only as prose inside the Problem Statement.

The level contract requires only mechanical docs (spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md; implementation-summary.md after implementation starts); handover.md, goal.md, timeline.md, decision-record.md and research/research.md are lazy addons, and acceptance-criteria.md is optional at Levels 2-3 with AC_CLOSURE as the separate gate.
The phase level requires spec.md alone and its section-gate table declares the 'problem' anchor required for phase spec.md, so the declared contract does name the purpose section at parent level.

Required-section enforcement for stamped documents exists: ANCHORS_VALID requires every anchor whose template section is a required H2, but only when the document carries a v2.3+ SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE stamp; a v2.4 spec.md that deletes PROBLEM & PURPOSE fails with a named missing anchor.

The phase parent is explicitly exempt from ANCHORS_VALID ('Phase parent lean document set accepted'), and the sufficiency loop enforces missing anchors only for timeline.md and goal.md; a phase parent can therefore drop Problem & Purpose entirely and still validate.

No validation rule reads the purpose prose: grep counts for 'problem' are zero across the validator modules, and the only content-shaped checks are placeholder tokens and the non-empty-anchor-body check, so a vacuous purpose sentence passes.

goal.md is the only surface with a durable one-line statement of intent ('## 1. DURABLE DIRECTIVE / Objective'), its anchors are required whenever the file exists, and it is a lazy addon, so a packet that never asked for it has no durable directive.

The two successor-facing surfaces carry no purpose field: handover.md has no problem/purpose heading, the _memory.continuity block has recent_action, next_safe_action, blockers, key_files, completion_pct, open_questions and answered_questions but no purpose key, and acceptance-criteria.md has no purpose column.
